prize_parts.citation: for developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular basis of cereblon-mediated degraders

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation as the whole prize. Its core is a physical-chemical principle that can be stated plainly: a small molecule induces a ternary complex, and the cell's own ubiquitin machinery does the work, so activity depends on cooperativity and kinetics and not on occupancy. That is measurable, it has been reproduced across many independent laboratories for over two decades, and it is the one shortlisted idea that all eight members ranked at opening. Handa's identification of cereblon shows that the same principle explains the thalidomide-type glue degraders, and I think a citation built on induced proximity, with a PROTAC origin and a cereblon mechanism, describes one concept honestly. The round-1 exchange did not change my configuration, but it sharpened what I will defend: the citation must be written around the principle and its molecular basis, not around the number of drugs.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, which is the strongest argument for caution and I cannot dismiss it; Aili, Somfai, Zou and Brzezinski each press on it, and so should I. Three names leave out Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands are the weakest exclusion. Linke, Chabes and Aqvist argue that PROTACs and the cereblon strand are different discoveries, and if the committee agrees then my Handa slot is an attribution risk, not a strength. If the committee wants a PROTAC-only citation, I would accept Crews and Deshaies with Ciulli as third name before I would defend a citation that blurs the two strands. The evidence that would move me off B018 is a clear showing that medicinal-chemistry optimisation, and not the induced-proximity principle, is what the prize would reward.

responses.point: Linke pairs Liu-only base editing with Crews and Deshaies for PROTACs, and argues that the cereblon and glue story is a separate mechanism-of-action discovery that should be its own part if wanted.
responses.response: I take the glue-is-separate argument seriously, and it is the main place I could move. My reason for keeping Handa is that the thalidomide-type drugs are the only degraders with a long clinical history, and cereblon shows that induced proximity is a mechanism the cell can use with a chemically simple ligand, which is why the principle is general. But I accept that this is one concept with two histories and that the citation has to say so. On your own pairing, I do not dispute the clean Liu attribution. My reservation is the one I gave in round 1: base editing is an engineered deaminase fusion on the platform the 2020 prize recognised. You and I both concede that no degrader is approved, so on timing we are in the same position, and I would not use that point against B018 while accepting it for your second part.

responses.point: Somfai asks whether PROTAC design is new chemistry or medicinal-chemistry optimisation of ligand-linker-ligand compounds, and keeps B018 only as an alternative until there is approval or strong late-stage data.
responses.response: The linker and ligand optimisation is medicinal chemistry, and I agree it is not the prize-worthy part. The new content is that productive degradation depends on ternary-complex cooperativity and on the geometry of E3 and target contact, which is thermodynamics and kinetics that can be measured and that explain why some degraders work and others do not. That is a physical-chemical result about induced proximity, and it is what I would want the citation to name. I also respect your point that C-N coupling is mature and cleanly attributed. My difficulty is that, after 2010, the committee would have to explain what is new beyond ligand control of the Pd cycle, and your own answer, ligand control of reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes, is a real refinement but still a refinement within a recognised paradigm. I keep B002 as my alternative for its maturity, not as a competitor in novelty.

responses.point: Aili prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles with base editing, citing population-scale clinical proof, and asked for my view on whether Cullis and Hope without Madden is a defensible cut.
responses.response: I think the science is as good as you say: pKa tuning, charge-dependent phase behaviour and fusogenic structure are lipid self-assembly in the sense I work in, and the 2023 Medicine prize made the RNA tolerated while the lipids made it deliverable. My answer on Cullis and Hope without Madden is that I cannot defend it. The formulation concept, the lipid optimisation and the library work came from different groups, and each cut will be contested, which is why I keep B016 as my first alternative and not my preferred part. I also hold a small bias, since this is my field, and I would rather say that than let it push B016 ahead of a better-attributed candidate. If someone makes a clear argument for who established the ionizable-lipid design principle, I would reconsider it.

responses.point: Aqvist holds Crews, Deshaies and Handa, is open to swapping Handa for Ciulli, and says phase separation is a maturity problem and not a criticism of the science.
responses.response: I agree on both points. On phase separation, I placed it first at opening and I still think it is the strongest new idea of molecular organisation on the list, but you are right that the physiological definition and relevance of condensates are unsettled and that credit is wider than my opening suggested; that is why it is no longer in my alternatives. On Handa against Ciulli, I think the answer depends on how the citation is framed. A citation about the induced-proximity principle and its mechanism needs the cereblon work, while a PROTAC-concept citation needs Ciulli and not Handa. I would not mix them, and I would accept either honest framing.

uncertainties: Whether the lack of an approved degrader should delay recognition, and what evidence of clinical benefit the committee would regard as sufficient.
Whether the PROTAC and cereblon strands are one achievement or two, and whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name if a one-concept citation is chosen.
Whether the committee finds a defensible attribution for ionizable lipid nanoparticles, which I would otherwise weigh heavily.
Whether my own preference for physical-chemical explanations leads me to overvalue ternary-complex thermodynamics as new chemistry relative to medicinal-chemistry design.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My lipid self-assembly work is close to B016 and to the physical chemistry behind B052, and I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, but I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited name. I note this for B016 in particular, which I list only as an alternative.
